newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras approves urgent coffee road repair funds.
newsitem.headline: Honduras approves urgent coffee road repair funds.

text.p: Honduras Thursday approved emergency funds to repair roads in coffee growing regions to lessen crop losses after being hit by severe storms over the last 10 days.

Oscar Guzman, vice president of the Honduras Association of Coffee Growers, announced the government's Coffee Fund approved 10 million lempiras ($796,000) for the urgent repairs of roads and access tracks in coffee areas.
Guzman said the Santa Barbara region in northeast Honduras was particularly badly affected.

"In that zone, the problems caused by the storms are serious because they have affected the coffee crop and we are worried that if no action is taken, the country will be hit by a fall in dollar earnings from coffee sales," Guzman said.
"Beans that have fallen from tres have to be picked up rapidly and the coffee taken to market to minimise the losses," said another goverment economy official.
Aside coffee, banana plantations and other crops were also affected by the two weather systems, one Hurricane Marcos and another tropical depression, sources said.
Mario Canahuati, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of of Cortes, said 800 hectares of banana and 1,000 hectares of basic grains were flooded in the storms.

Canahuati, whose group is the coastal banana region, said the flooded plantations belonged mostly to U.S. firm Tela Railroad Company. The U.S. Standard Fruit Company also suffered similar losses in the Aguan valley, he added.
Earlier, the president of the Association of Honduran Coffee Exporters said there had been damage but it was top early to estimate to what extent.
"We have had too much rain and there will be damage, but it very difficult to estimate to what extent so soon after the storms," Osmond Maduro told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Maduro said the low-lying coffee growing zones of Copan, Ocotepeque and Cortes were especially hit, with the Honduran 1996-1997 harvest (November-March) just starting.
Honduras was expected to harvest a 3 million 46-kg bag harvest this year similar to the output recorded last cycle.
Maduro said it was "very likely" that rains caused beans to fall from trees. He added that infrastructure damage, largely to plantation access roads, had already been reported.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
